key_insight: Jellyfish feeding efficiency is predicted to peak at the transition from Stokes pumping to inertial prey transport, where self-generated vortex rings enhance prey capture.
engineering_relevance: These findings could inform bio-inspired underwater pumps and robots that balance fluid transport against actuation energy.
method: Study prey capture versus energy spent deforming the jellyfish surface.
Develop a feeding-efficiency landscape spanning viscous and inertial transport.
Compare predictions with reported species traits and moon jellyfish observations.
evidence_signal: Predictions explain reported jellyfish sizes and beat frequencies across taxa, while observations of Aurelia aurita support vortex-ring-dominated transport.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation metrics, and experimental support is reported only for moon jellyfish.
paper_title: Vortex rings shape the feeding-efficiency landscape of jellyfish
